title: The size and agility of his hands
summary: Dance asks about his hands; he says they are large, can reach more than a tenth, and have been developed by playing.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It seems to me that nimbleness must have been something that you cultivated because compared to some piano players, your hands are small compared to an Earl Hines or --
I don't know, you haven't looked at them.
No, I wasn't looking (Inaudible). Are they not big?
No, my hands are very large.
Are they?
Look there.
Now what is your reach then?
Well, I can reach way over a tenth.
You can?
Yes, I can reach actually --
I am surprised.
Not practical, because a tenth is just about the most practical thing that you can reach.
Yes.
And I can reach a tenth very easily, which in fact is very comfortable for me to reach a tenth.
Were your hands always well developed or did that -- or did you develop them? To play.
Well, naturally they were developed more from playing music.
Yes.
Naturally, practicing on the scales.
That was very fortunate, wasn't it.
Oh, yes, of course. But I think most all musicians have well coordinated hands on any instrument.
Yes.
Your hands become stronger and more agile.
Yes.
Because they have to be.
Yes.
It's coordination of your --
Continual use of them, yes.
Right. It's a coordination of your mind and your fingers, and they must be simultaneous.
Right.
But I don't think mine are faster than
anybody else's, however, as I said, it's just -- it's part of your training, you know.
